model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the average performance across five datasets (NQ, TQA, zsRE, T-rex, HQA) for three different methods: Standard, CInGS (w/), and CInGS, under two conditions: "With Context" and "Without Context". The vertical axis represents "Average Performance" on a linear scale from 0 to 60, with tick marks at intervals of 10. The horizontal axis categorizes the data into two groups: "With Context" (left) and "Without Context" (right), each containing three bars corresponding to the three methods. For the "With Context" condition, the blue bars represent the Standard method (approximately 58), CInGS (w/) (approximately 55), and CInGS (approximately 53), all showing high performance. For the "Without Context" condition, the purple bars show lower performance: Standard (approximately 45), CInGS (w/) (approximately 46), and CInGS (approximately 44). The legend indicates that "Standard" is represented by a dark gray bar with a dotted pattern, "CInGS (w/)" by a solid blue bar, and "CInGS" by a solid purple bar. The bars are arranged in the same order for both conditions, with no visual emphasis or annotations on individual bars. The chart visually demonstrates that performance is consistently higher when context is provided, and that the Standard method generally outperforms the CInGS variants in both conditions.
